To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of VGCC and the number of presynapse sites are related to the number of synapses in hair cells.
the size of presynaptic active zones and the number of calcium channels at these active zones are correlated with innervation density among neurally located hair cells of the avian cochlea.

the density of voltage-gated Ca2+ channels in hair cells of the avian basilar papilla is correlated with the number of presynapses and the total cross-sectional area of presynaptic active zones, which in turn are correlated with the number and size of afferent synapses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the structure of hair cells is related to their synaptic function.
the relationship between the number of calcium channels and release sites and their role in transmitter release at synapse.
how calcium channels are expressed at release sites and how these channels contribute to transmitter release in hair cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hair cells are not identical in the way that they are innervated.
the number, distribution, size, and type of calcium channels in hair cells are correlated to their afferent innervations.
hair cells of the basilar papilla are innervated by afferent nerve fibers that express a high density of dihydropyrydine-sensitive VGCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the synaptic architecture of hair cells may be a critical determinant of their physiological properties and that the synaptic architecture varies among hair cells in a systematic way that correlates with their afferent innervations.
calcium channel expression is a function of both the number and size of release sites in hair cells.
the number and distribution of calcium channels in hair cells is matched to the number and distribution release sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hair cell synaptic architecture is not static, but rather it is dynamic and can vary among hair cells in a manner that is consistent with the functional demands placed on each cell.
hair cell excitability is determined by afferent synapse architecture.
the size of the presynaptic active zone (PDB) is an important determinant of the number of VGCC that will be found at a given release site.
